title: Etale localizations above a valuation closed point are valuation domains
statement: Let $A$ be a valuation domain [def-trf-valuation-ring], with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$. Let $B$ be a commutative $A$-algebra such that $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be a prime ideal whose inverse image in $A$ is $\mathfrak m_A$. Then the natural homomorphism $A\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ is injective and local, and $B_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a valuation domain. Here local means that the inverse image of the maximal ideal $\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak q}$ is $\mathfrak m_A$. There is no henselian, Noetherian, rank, or module-finiteness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0ASJ, lemma-etale-extension-valuation-ring, statement and first proof paragraph, lines 37479--37492: the assertion that A is a subring of B_q and that B_q is a valuation ring. Only the valuation-domain assertion is needed, not the additional weakly-unramified conclusion.

proof.text: Apply clauses (1) and (4) of [det-pe-morphisms-etale-comparison] to the given affine scheme morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Thus $A\to B$ is flat and its multiplication $B\otimes_A B\to B$ is flat: this is precisely weak etaleness of the ring map in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra].

source.place: Tag 0ASJ, lemma-etale-extension-valuation-ring, first proof paragraph (valuation assertion only).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flat-localized-field-descent] with $R=A$, $S=B$, $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_A$ and the specified $\mathfrak q$. Its hypotheses hold by step 1 and the contraction hypothesis. It gives an injective local map $A_{\mathfrak m_A}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$. Since $A$ is local, every denominator outside $\mathfrak m_A$ is a unit. Hence the localization map $A\to A_{\mathfrak m_A}$ is an isomorphism, with inverse $a/s\mapsto a s^{-1}$. Its composite with the displayed map is the natural $a\mapsto a/1$, which is therefore injective and local. Explicitly $a/1\in\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak q}$ exactly when $a$ maps into $\mathfrak q$, exactly when $a\in\mathfrak m_A$.

source.place: Tag 0ASJ, lemma-etale-extension-valuation-ring, first proof paragraph (valuation assertion only).

proof.text: Apply the local-ring clause of [lem-trf-weak-dimension-one-valuation-criterion] to the valuation domain $A$. It supplies a flat resolution of length at most one for every $A$-module. By the final clause of [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-tor] and step 1, the same bound holds for every $B$-module. No finiteness of those modules or of the localized algebra is required.

source.place: Tag 0ASJ, lemma-etale-extension-valuation-ring, first proof paragraph (valuation assertion only).

proof.text: Apply the implication (i) $\Rightarrow$ (ii) of [lem-trf-weak-dimension-one-valuation-criterion] to $R=B$ and the prime $\mathfrak q$. The bound established in step 3 gives that $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is a valuation domain, including that it is an integral domain. Together with step 2 this proves every assertion.
